question: What is the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 10 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a triangle = (Base × Height) ÷ 2

Area = (12 × 10) ÷ 2 = 60 cm²

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Base of the triangle = 12 cm, Height of the triangle = 10 cm

Formula Used: Area = 1/2 × Base × Height

 
 
• A B C Height = 10 cm Base = 12 cm Area = 1/2 × 12 × 10 = 60 cm² 

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 12 × 10

⇒ Area = 6 × 10

⇒ Area = 60 cm²

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

When all three sides (a, b, c) are known, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semi-perimeter.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For an equilateral triangle with side 'a', Area = (√3 / 4) × a².

Right-angled Triangle

Area = 1/2 × Product of the two sides containing the right angle (Base × Perpendicular).
